newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WIN TO LEAD SERIES 3-2.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WIN TO LEAD SERIES 3-2.

text.p: Australia held their nerve in the field on Tuesday to win a tense one-day international against South Africa by eight runs.

Replying to Australia's 258 for seven, the home side could only manage 250 for eight in their 50 overs. Australia now hold a 3-2 lead in the seven-match series with the remaining games being played in Pretoria on Thursday and Bloemfontein on Sunday.

South Africa suffered a top order collapse that saw them reeling at 31 for three, but a fourth wicket century stand between Daryll Cullinan, who made 53, and Jacques Kallis, 55, put them back in contention.
After three more wickets fell quickly Hansie Cronje and Shaun Pollock put on 73 for the seventh wicket.

Needing seven an over off the last 10 the pair were well on course with five overs to go. But master leg-spinner Shane Warne returned to have Pollock caught at mid-wicket off a full toss for 40 and Cronje could not coax the winning runs from the tail. South Africa's captain finished 40 not out.

Australia's score was built around a career-best 89 in 114 balls from Tasmanian left-hander Michael DiVenuto. He put on 93 for the first wicket with Greg Blewett, whose 36 was the second highest score.
Michael Bevan weighed in with 32 from 35 balls and there was a sparkling 26 in 17 from Adam Gilchrist but the 258 total looked within reach of the hosts.
The Australian bowlers grabbed the early initiative as Adam Dale trapped the dangerous Herschelle Gibbs lbw for 22 and Adam Bacher was caught off the back of the bat for six.
Derek Crookes, promoted as the pinch hitter, was then run out for a duck by a direct hit.

Home hopes rose as Cullinan and Kallis batted with increasing freedom for their 101 stand. Kallis hit successive sixes off short balls from Bevan and drove Jason Gillespie high over long-on for another.
But Gillespie had his revenge when Kallis hit a catch to Steve Waugh and despite heroics from Pollock and Cronje the visitors held on to win more comfortably than the margin might suggest.
